tools.name: search_properties
tools.description:
Search PropertyList's full Spanish property MLS by structured filters.
Use for queries that translate cleanly to fields: bedrooms, bathrooms,
price ceiling, property type, area name. For free-form briefs use
find_properties_by_description instead.

Returns a paginated list with summary text plus str

tools.name: find_properties_by_description
tools.description:
Match Spanish properties from a free-form description of what the
user wants. Best for vague, conditional, or lifestyle-heavy briefs
("3-bed near a good international school, flexible on budget if
there's a sea view"). The matcher translates the brief into one
to three parallel structured searches a

tools.name: autocomplete_location
tools.description:
Look up Spanish property areas (city, suburb, urbanisation) by
free-text name. Returns up to 10 matches with id, name, and the
parent province/city. Use this to resolve place names before
calling search_properties, especially for common spellings like
'Nueva Andalucia' (vs 'Nueva Andalucía') or 'Mar

tools.name: get_property
tools.description:
Fetch the full record for one PropertyList listing by its reference
code (the human-readable id like 'PLE-12345'). Use this once the
user has settled on a listing from search_properties or
find_properties_by_description and wants details or photos. To
contact the listing agency, use submit_enquiry -

tools.name: area_market_summary
tools.description:
Return aggregate market context for a Spanish area: number of active
listings, median price, mean price, median €/m², and the count
broken down by bedroom band. Filterable by property type and search
type (for-sale / for-rent / holiday-rentals). Use this before
recommending a price or commenting on

tools.name: list_agencies
tools.description:
Find PropertyList agencies (estate agents) in a given Spanish area,
ranked by how many active listings they carry there. Returns up to
10 agencies with name, location, listing count, and a public URL
the user can visit. Use this after a buyer has narrowed in on an
area and wants to know which agenci

tools.name: verified_valuation
tools.description:
Get a valuation for a property or area from recorded market data, not
asking prices. Returns the €/m² for the municipality and segment, an
indicative valuation when you give a size (build_sqm) or a listing
reference, and a content-hashed attestation URL the figure can be cited
from.

tools.description:
Submit an enquiry (lead) about a specific listing on behalf of a prospective
buyer or tenant. Use this once the user has chosen a property and wants the
agency to contact them. The listing agency receives the enquiry in their CRM
and follows up directly.

tools.name: my_leads
tools.description:
List recent enquiries (leads) for YOUR agency's CRM - newest first.
Use when the agent asks what has just come in (e.g. "what came in
today?").

This is the enquiry inbox: an enquiry that arrived from the portal,
a website or a microsite. Once an agent starts working a person
they live on a pipeline

tools.name: my_pipeline
tools.description:
List the cards on YOUR agency's CRM pipeline boards (Kanban), with
each board's own stage names and card counts.

Boards: lead, buyer, seller, tenant, nurture (each card is a
contact) and property (each card is a listing). Stage names are
whatever the agency renamed them to, so read them from the re

tools.name: find_contacts
tools.description:
Search YOUR agency's CRM contacts by name, company, email or phone.
Use to look a person up before logging a note or to check if they're
already in the CRM. Requires an agency API key; only ever searches the
calling agency's own contacts.

tools.name: my_listings
tools.description:
List YOUR agency's own property listings (newest first), optionally
filtered by status or a specific reference. Use for "show my listings"
/ "is reference X still online?". Requires an agency API key; only ever
returns the calling agency's own properties.

tools.name: create_contact
tools.description:
Add a new contact to YOUR agency's CRM. Use when the agent wants to
save a person (buyer, owner, enquirer). If a contact with the same
email already exists it is returned rather than duplicated. The contact
is created unassigned and flagged as needing attention so it surfaces
in the CRM. Requires an

tools.name: create_listing
tools.description:
Start a new property listing in YOUR agency's CRM from a description.
Use when the agent is describing a property they have taken on and
wants it in the system.

Creates a DRAFT. It is never published and never appears on the
portal from here: the agent adds photographs and the energy rating
in the

tools.name: log_note
tools.description:
Log a note against a contact or a listing in YOUR agency's CRM (e.g.
record a call outcome or a viewing). Provide the note text plus a
contact_id (from find_contacts) and/or a property reference. The note
appears on the contact/property timeline. Requires an agency API key.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_property, list_agencies, verified_valuation, submit_enquiry, my_leads, find_contacts · Private data: search_properties, get_property, submit_enquiry, my_leads, my_pipeline, find_contacts, my_listings, create_contact, create_listing, log_note · Public sink: get_property, submit_enquiry, find_contacts, create_contact.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_property, list_agencies, verified_valuation, submit_enquiry, my_leads, find_contacts · Private data: search_properties, get_property, submit_enquiry, my_leads, my_pipeline, find_contacts, my_listings, create_contact, create_listing, log_note · Public sink: get_property, submit_enquiry, find_contacts, create_contact

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_properties" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
